title: Inconsistency between facet widgets for hasResults
body:
We sometimes use `facetValues.length`, some others `nbHits` (or even `hits.length`, leading to even more inconsistency).
I think we should:
- either rename `hideContainerWhenNoResults` to `hideContainerWhenNoRefinements` for them and use `facetValues`
- or expose both, with `hideContainerWhenNoRefinements = false` and `hideContainerWhenNoResults = true`

WDYT?

comments.body: @Jerskouille Is this still accurate with the refactoring on the `autoHide` decorator?
Yes, that's how I saw it, but I didn't fix it.

I think most of the time what you want is "hideContainerWhenNoResults". Because if there's no results then there's no facets?

So maybe we should always use nbHits internally for consistency if it's ok with you.
(removed the bug label, this is not a bug right now)

The behaviour can be really different as soon as we have `null` on some facet values. Some blocks might be displayed when there is actually nothing in it.
And it is actually a bug since some are using `nbHits` (`price-ranges`, `toggle`), and others are using `facetValues.length` (`refinement-list`, `menu`, `hierarchical-menu`), meaning that they don't behave consistently when there are `null` values.
And with `hitsPerPage: 0`, it's also inconsistent, hence the `bug` tag.

Ok better understood the bug (facet values containing null) => leads to a bug.

`hideContainerWhenNoResults` still seems ok as for naming and having only one option. Maybe we just need to ensure to only check the relevant information to hide/display the widget (which is the number of available refinements in the end).
So the actual bug is that in some widget we keep rendering them even when the refinement array is empty right?

I actually don't know. Maybe it's what we want.
It's more that the parameter name is inconsistent with the behaviour.

By the way, I'm already introducing `hideContainerWhenNoRefinements` in #404 and #405 .
But it is actually not doing the same thing than what I'm proposing here, the one in both issues linked before is used to check if a refinement has been made by the user or not.

Ah indeed hideContainerWhenNoRefinements would then have two meanings. Maybe we should just have "autoHide: true/false" like we had at the begining then handle the implementation differently.

I am not sure the user need so much detail, it should just hide when it's obvious (either no results or no refinements or no refinements made).

> I'm ok with an autoHideContainer.

:v: WFM nice
